target.projectDescription: openapi-python-client 0.5.2 (pyproject.toml; __version__ resolved via importlib.metadata) - a Python CLI tool that generates a modern Python client library from an OpenAPI 3 document. Core flow: openapi_python_client/__main__.py calls the typer app in cli.py; the app callback reads --config (Optional[pathlib.Path] -> _process_config -> Config.load_from_path -> yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) - project_name_override / package_name_override / class_overrides {class_name, module_name}); the `generate` and `update` commands take --url or --path; create_new_client/update_existing_client (openapi_python_client/__init__.py) call _get_document (httpx.get(url).content for --url, path.read_bytes() for --path) then yaml.safe_load into a dict; GeneratorData.from_dict (parser/openapi.py) validates via oai.OpenAPI.parse_obj (pydantic) and builds Schemas (model/enum references from schema names/titles via Reference.from_ref -> pascal_case/snake_case) and EndpointCollections keyed by operation tag; Project.__init__ computes project_name from openapi.title (or config project_name_override), project_dir = Path.cwd() / project_name, package_dir = project_dir / package_name; Project.build() mkdirs project_dir/package_dir/models/api/async_api and writes every generated file via pathlib write_text (module file names from model/enum reference.module_name and from the RAW operation tag: api_dir / f"{tag}.py"); Project.update() checks package_dir.is_dir() then shutil.rmtree(package_dir) and regenerates; _reformat() runs subprocess.run('isort .'/'black .', cwd=project_dir, shell=True).

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: The audit target is the openapi-python-client CLI itself, so the untrusted-input boundaries are (1) the REMOTE OpenAPI document body fetched over HTTP - httpx.get(url) __init__.py:71 / response.content :72 / yaml.safe_load :80 - whenever the operator points --url at a server they do not control (fetching external specs is the tool's core use case, so the document is treated as the dominant attacker-influenced input: info.title becomes project_name -> project_dir = Path.cwd() / project_name -> mkdir/rmtree/write_text targets; schema titles and #/components/schemas/ ref leaf names become model/enum reference.module_name -> models_dir / f"{module_name}.py" write targets via Reference.from_ref + pascal_case/snake_case; operation.tags become the RAW f"{tag}.py" module file names under api/ and async_api/ with NO transformation); (2) the CLI-selected local OpenAPI document file - path.read_bytes() __init__.py:76 (operator-trust level: the person invoking the tool chooses the file, but its content is external data of the same shape as the URL case); (3) the config file - yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) config.py:34 with project_name_override / package_name_override / class_overrides {class_name, module_name} (operator-trust level, same judgment as (2)); (4) the typer CLI boundary itself - the url/path/config Option parameters of cli()/generate()/update() (cli.py:34-38, 97-99, 115-117) and _process_config(path) (cli.py:20) - OPERATOR-TRUST level: the person invoking the CLI is the same trust domain as the options they pass; emitted for labeling to classify, NOT automatically attacker sources; (5) environment variables - NOT observed anywhere in the package (no os.environ/os.getenv) - no env family emitted. The filesystem-operation channels are concentrated in openapi_python_client/__init__.py Project: mkdir (project_dir :109, package_dir :146, models_dir :186, api_dir :218, async_api_dir :223 - receivers built from Path.cwd()/project_name), write_text (15 sites :151/:154/:160/:172/:181/:192/:197/:204/:208/:214/:220/:225/:229/:235/:237 - the module-name sites :197/:204 and the RAW-tag sites :235/:237 have REMOTE-name-controlled receivers), shutil.rmtree(package_dir) :125 (update() - the package_dir path is title-derived), read_bytes :76 / read_text config.py:34, is_dir guard :122, the pathlib '/' join family (20 Div sites, all in __init__.py, of which :95/:98/:196/:203/:234/:236 append the remote-controlled components), Path.cwd() :95, and subprocess.run(..., cwd=project_dir, shell=True) :133/:136 (isort/black rewrite files under the Python-supplied cwd). There is NO builtin open(), NO os.path.* call, NO archive/zipfile/tarfile usage, NO upload/multipart filename handling, and NO static-file/file-response serving in the audited code.

guardsAndEvidence.containmentChecks: NONE observed. There is no base-directory containment check, no realpath/abspath/normpath canonicalization, no '..' rejection, no basename extraction, no path-prefix validation anywhere in the audited package (grep confirms zero os.path usage). The only name shaping before file-name use: project_name = openapi.title.replace(' ', '-').lower() + '-client' (__init__.py:94 - cosmetic only, does not affect '/' or '..'), module_name = snake_case(pascal_case(ref leaf or schema title)) (parser/reference.py:25/:30 via stringcase - case reshaping only, does not strip path separators), and the tag which is used COMPLETELY RAW in api_dir / f"{tag}.py" (__init__.py:234/:236).
guardsAndEvidence.existenceChecks: project_dir.mkdir() catches FileExistsError (__init__.py:110 - build() refuses to overwrite, an existence guard not a traversal guard); Project.update() checks package_dir.is_dir() (:122) before rmtree (:125) - a TOCTOU-shaped check-then-delete with no path validation.
guardsAndEvidence.overrideMechanisms: Reference.from_ref consults the class_overrides map (parser/reference.py:27, populated from the config file) - a name-substitution mechanism, not a path guard; Config parsing is wrapped in a bare try/except in _process_config (cli.py:26-29) which only converts parse failures into a CLI error.
guardsAndEvidence.toctouEvidence: is_dir() check at __init__.py:122 followed by shutil.rmtree at :125 - the classic check-then-act window on the package_dir path (title/config-derived).
guardsAndEvidence.trustBoundaryJudgment: The OpenAPI document CONTENT (via --url fetch or --path file) is the genuine untrusted boundary: consuming externally-authored specs is the tool's entire purpose, and document fields (info.title, schema titles/refs, operation.tags) directly determine created/deleted/written filesystem paths under the process CWD. The CLI options themselves (--url/--path/--config) and the config file are OPERATOR-TRUST level (same trust domain as the invoking user) - recorded as candidates for the labeling step to classify, NOT automatically treated as attacker sources. The subprocess isort/black channel and httpx.get URL are noted as cross-pass material (Pass 2 / Pass 3) but their file-effect scoping / content boundary is emitted for Pass 1.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (one at a time, sequential) + codeql bqrs decode --format=csv (NOT database analyze / SARIF); both are plain multi-column select queries on purpose: @kind problem is the wrong shape for candidate tables and @kind table is not assumed to exist
extraction.columnContract: identical order in both queries and consistent with the prior projects in this series (dfetch et al.): node (location-backed AST node), role ('source_candidate'/'sink_candidate'), callable, flow_kind, receiver, moduleHint (variable intentionally named moduleHint - `module` is not a valid QL variable name), arg_index (0-based positional index; -1 when the value is the receiver, the return value, a keyword argument, or an operator form), file (via Location API), line (1-based start line), match_kind ('api' for resolved API calls / 'ast' for syntax-level matches)
extraction.expectedMatchKind: all rows are expected to decode as match_kind 'ast': httpx, yaml, pydantic, typer, jinja2, stringcase, shutil and pathlib are external/stdlib modules not part of the database (only openapi_python_client + tests are), and the remaining channels are instance members on local variables (path.write_text, project_dir.mkdir, package_dir.is_dir, response.content) or operator forms (the Div joins); the match_kind column is kept for cross-project contract consistency
extraction.exclusions: /tests/, /end_to_end_tests/ (incl. golden-master generated client and fastapi_app fixture), /openapi-python-client-db/ (the CodeQL database nested inside the source tree) - applied to every row of both queries; openapi_python_client/templates is kept in scope (only templates/types.py is a .py file there and it contains no file operations, so no rows are expected from it)
